subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for an armoured 6-wheel convoy hauler with a sealed cargo pod, aiming for a low-poly cyberpunk style with neon accents and SVG decal textures like hazard stripes and runes, keeping the implementation compact at around 400-500 lines while staying correct against the SDK API.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: a chassis root joint, six wheel joints with steering on the front pair, a pod lid hatch, and a turret with yaw and pitch for a roof gun, figuring out wheel orientation and positioning along the chassis length with front, cab, and pod sections.

I'm settling on paint and color choices, reusing a panelled metal style from the clockwork kit for the hull finish.

I'm designing a custom grime paint that blends dark navy with a lighter top and dirt accumulation near the bottom using noise and smoothstep. For textures I'm planning hazard stripes, a corporate logo emblem reading "KUROGANE LOGISTICS," a glowing cyan HUD-style windscreen with neon reflections, and possibly a neon kanji sign for extra detail.

For surface decals I'm skipping risky fonts in favor of simple latin text like "SEALED" and "CARGO 07-K," plus a warning triangle decal, a sensor-eye visor marking, a circular glowing seal glyph, and a number plate. These will attach as planes on each flat surface with the correct outward direction and orientation so the text reads properly from outside the pod.

Now I'm working out the chassis and cab geometry: frame rails and a belly plate box for the base, then extruding a cab profile along the side view using absolute z/y coordinates to shape the wedge-like front cab with bevels and proper centering.

I'll skip detailed wheel arches but add simple fender boxes above the wheels to suggest coverage, positioning the wheels slightly wider than the cab body so they poke out a bit from the sides, which is fine for a stylized look.

For the windscreen, I'm working out the geometry for the raked front slope—calculating the center point, normal direction, and plane dimensions so the glass panel sits flush against the angled surface between the hood and roof line.

I'm adding glowing neon HUD texture to the windscreen, then positioning darker reflective glass panels on the side windows near the front of the cab, and planning glowing strip headlights at the front.

For the front face itself, I'm placing a decal plane near the nose with slit headlights and a central glowing visor-eye, plus a lower grille and bumper box, and sketching a plough with spike teeth along the ground for the front ram.

Shaping the plough outline...

For the roof, I'm thinking through sensor array details, a glowing light bar, antenna spikes, and a turret assembly with a base drum, housing box, and twin barrels with a pitch joint.

For the joints, I'm sorting out hinge directions for yaw and pitch, following the existing conventions where pitch aims along the bone's forward axis. Then I'll move on to the cargo pod, a sealed capsule-shaped container on the back of the vehicle.

Designing the pod as an octagonal prism swept along a horizontal path, with flat end caps and painted color, sized to sit flush against the chassis top.

I'm checking clearances: the pod bottom lands right at the chassis deck level, which sits above the wheel tops, so the pod overhangs the wheels slightly—I'll need fender boxes underneath to bridge that gap visually.

For the sweep geometry, I'm confirming the pod uses a straight two-point path with octagonal cross-section, then adding rib bands around it using wider-radius short sweeps along the same axis, oriented so their flat faces point outward correctly. I'll color the ribs dark steel and give the pod body a deep teal-black panelled finish.

Now I'm designing the pod's rear hatch: a grimy dark-blue panelled base texture, then a sealed door with glowing red lock lights and crossing locking bars, built as an octagonal cylinder part attached via a hinge joint so it reads visually as a rear access door.

I'm also figuring out where the flat octagon side faces land so I can place "KUROGANE HAULAGE" logo decals and warning labels symmetrically on both sides.

For the cyberpunk feel, I'm adding neon underglow rods in cyan along the chassis bottom, magenta accent strips on the pod ribs, and glowing window trim, plus a hazard-striped top panel with embedded light strips.

For the wheels, I'm building each one from a tread-blocked tire, a rim, hub, lug nuts, and a glowing cyan neon ring on the outer face, repeated across all six wheels along with mud flaps and suspension details.

Working out tread block positioning and rotation math...

Now I'm laying out the wheel positions along the hauler's chassis—front steering axle near z=2.9, mid and rear axles further back—and checking tire widths against the cab span to make sure the hauler looks proportionate rather than too wide.

Adding cab details now: light bar, antennas, mirrors, exhaust stacks, step ladders, headlights, grille, sensor dome, fuel tanks, skirt plates, cable runs between cab and pod, and armor plates with bolt rows. Still need mud flaps and tow hooks.

Working out the rear bumper with glowing tail lights, decal placement for a door number and plate, and detailing the cab door itself -- seams, handle, window pane, and raised door panel geometry positioned precisely along the cab's side walls.

Now I'm setting up the paint system for the hull, defining a panelled texture with rivets and a base color that blends charcoal-blue tones with grime and lighting variation using noise, plus a palette of ink, steel, and neon cyan/magenta/amber accent colors.

I'm designing the side logo decal as an SVG panel with rounded dark background, cyan border, bold "KUROGANE" branding text, a subtitle, hexagon emblem, and barcode graphic, tuned so the glow effect gives it a neon look against the dark panel.

Now I'm planning out the remaining textures: a circular seal with concentric rings and runes, hazard diagonal stripes, a windscreen texture with HUD lines and a reticle, a front face with headlight slits and a red scanning visor eye, a door texture, and a rear tail plate with a light bar and plate number "HX-0742".

I'm also figuring out the roof turret assembly placement -- yaw base, ring housing, pitch cradle, twin barrels with glowing muzzle tips, ammo boxes, and a sensor ball with a red lens -- plus positioning the lightbar on the sloped roof near the turret without overlapping it.

I'm adding glowing magenta and cyan segments to that lightbar, a back-mounted antenna whip cluster, and a rubber bellows connector joining the cab and rear pod with cables to cover the small gap between them.

Checking the proportions now—the pod towers noticeably higher than the cab roof, which gives it a dominant, guard-sealed look with the turret tucked safely in front of it. I'm also detailing the pod's front bulkhead with a chamfered cap and lights, making sure the overhang clears the cab's back wall properly.

Now I'm figuring out the cradle setup underneath the pod: a deck box supporting it with strap bands and ratchets at each rib position, plus small buckle housings with glowing amber LEDs along the sides for that mechanical, secured look. I'm also adding hazard tie-down plates across the pod's top surface.

Writing hazard decal texture...

I'm also adding cyan underglow rods along the chassis edges for a subtle lighting accent underneath.

Now I'm double-checking the wheel geometry — making sure the hub radius, tire carcass, and tread blocks all align so the bottom edge sits flush at ground level.

Overall height comes to roughly 3.5-4m with antennas, which feels about right for a realistic truck scale. Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders to streamline building out the ~300 parts.

Writing part placement helpers...

Still writing SVG code...

I'm placing the hazard stripe panels on the plow and bumpers, then designing a windshield HUD with a reticle, speed readout, lane paths, and a subtle diagonal reflection over an opaque dark background, framed with a border.

Now I'm sketching the vehicle face with slanted amber/white headlight polygons, a glowing red visor scanner, lower grille bars, and a small "KG-07" label, followed by a door plaque with amber chevrons and lettering, and a tail panel with a red light band.

Writing the top warning panel with rotated "DO NOT OPEN" text, a hazard triangle, and chevron arrows, then starting the actual code for the scene builder in TypeScript using Three.js.

Still writing builder imports and paint logic...

Defining chassis geometry...

Working out the hood slope and vent slat geometry, figuring out the rotation angle needed so the vents align with the hood's tilt from front to back.

Now I'm finishing the hood ribs and cab bellows details, then positioning the front nose face plane—sizing it around 2.1 by 0.58 centered at y 1.22, tilted slightly toward +z with a small bevel.

I'm also sorting out the bumper placement below the nose, checking that its box dimensions and position merge cleanly with the plow top without awkward gaps or overlaps.

Adding fenders over the wheels with outer lip boxes, plus dark mud flaps behind each one, and now I'm placing steel fuel tank cylinders between the rear axles.

Positioning the exhaust stacks just outside the cab, checking the gap between the pod and cab walls so the stack radius clears both surfaces.

Adding a bellows connector box with ribs between the cab and pod, then two thin cable sweeps linking the cab back wall to the pod front using curved catmull paths for a natural hose-like droop.

Now I'm building the main pod body as an octagonal sweep extruded along its length, then adding a series of ribbed bands at intervals along the pod using slightly larger radius flat-capped sweeps so they read as raised structural rings. I'm leaving neon accents on the ribs for later and considering where to place a side logo decal on the flat pod face.

I'm checking spacing though — the gaps between ribs look too tight for a logo of that length, so I'm reworking the rib positions along the z-axis to leave a clear flat section for the decal while keeping the end ribs anchoring the pod.

For the logo plane itself, I'm fixing the aspect ratio mismatch by setting a wider SVG viewBox and repositioning the hexagon icon, text, and barcode elements to fit the new proportions.

Now I'm working through the mirrored side (s=-1), checking that the plane's orientation and the local coordinate axes still produce correctly readable text when viewed from the negative-x direction, computing the right-vector via cross products to verify.

Then I'm shifting to the rear door geometry, figuring out the pod door joint placement, parent bone, rotation, and the cylinder dimensions needed so the octagonal door disc fits properly within the rear ribs' radius.

I'm adding the seal plane, glowing ring torus, locking bolts, hinge knuckles, and diagonal lock bars to the door assembly, then moving on to designing the rear bumper, tail light, and plate.

Adding more turret details...

Adding ammo boxes on the sides, a sensor sphere with a glowing lens up top, and a roof light bar with alternating cyan/magenta glow segments. I'm also placing whip antennas at the sides extending upward.

Now I'm sketching a dish antenna on the rear roof using a lathed outline to form the dish shape, angled to face up and back, plus a support post, and starting on the side mirrors.

Still writing mirror and door geometry...

I'm adjusting wheel positioning so the front wheels sit at x ±1.35 with proper width, aligning fenders and ensuring chassis width works with cab width so the wheel inner edge fits nicely under the cab.

Now I'm writing a wheel function that creates a hub joint, optionally adds a steering joint parent, then a rotation joint for the wheel itself, attaching tire and tread geometry to it. I'm building the tire as a flat cylinder with tread blocks arranged radially around it.

Adding rim and hub details...

Skipping headlight beams for now, I'm positioning the pod's top mark plane and sizing it against the rib boundaries to get the dimensions right, then adding vent/panel detail to the upper diagonal faces.

Now I'm figuring out where to place small amber lamp boxes on the diagonal faces — computing the octagon's flat-face center position and spacing a row of six lamps between the existing ribs, with each box rotated outward to match the face angle.

Working out placement for the hazard stripe plane on the lower diagonal face, computing its offset position along the normal and adjusting for the texture's orientation relative to the world up axis.

For the top plane, I need to switch the up vector to point along z instead, since this face's normal and orientation differ from the side logo plane. I'm calculating the correct local x axis via a cross product between the face normal and the up vector to ensure the texture aligns properly.

Working through this, right = -x direction for a viewer standing above looking down, which checks out. Then for the rear door seal, I'm redoing the same cross-product check for a plane facing -z, confirming the local x axis still comes out to -x for a viewer standing behind the truck looking forward with +y as up.

Verifying the cab front and windscreen orientations the same way, then moving to detailing the cab's side elements—the door plate, seams, handles, and decals—positioning them along the side face with specific offsets and sizes.

Checking the window placement above the door plate, then noting I'll skip over secondary details like armour plating, rear wall bellows, underglow rods, roof hatch, and the hood sensor since they're minor additions I can leave simple.

I'm adding randomized greeble boxes along the cradle deck sides, verifying the glow import path and part access work correctly, then applying a glow effect to a cyan-colored box.

I'm keeping the palette under the material limit by tracking distinct color names, then setting up helper functions for placing parts on the chassis bone and for building rods between points.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing SVG details...

I'm checking clearances between the plow, cab, and chassis so nothing overlaps, then adding a front bumper beam box for the chassis underside. Satisfied with the spatial layout, I'm ready to finalize the code.

Now I'm placing the remaining details: wheel hub coordinates for front, mid, and rear axles, fuel tanks, a rear plate, neon underglow rods with a cyan glow, door hinge joints, and front corner amber lamps. With these pieces settled, I'm ready to write out the full answer.
